title: Moving an Approved Authorization to Another Servicing Provider, Referrals and Authorizations
content:
Desk guidance for **Referrals and Authorizations**: a patient may ask to move an approved authorization to another servicing provider where the authorization type allows the patient to move it.

## Conditions for the change

The servicing provider can be changed only while the authorization's status is approved; this is read from the authorization's status in the system record. In addition, the new provider must be:

1. of a kind listed among the kinds of provider that may serve that type;
2. of the same specialty as the original servicing provider; and
3. in the patient's residence service area, or, when it is outside, the patient accepts that the access standards (the appointment-offer days and the drive-time minutes) no longer bind the region.

A patient may not move the authorization to a provider who has already declined the patient.

## Effect of the change

The change takes effect on the date it is made. The units remaining and the validity span carry over unchanged, and units already used stay used.

## Judgement checklist

| Check | Must hold |
|---|---|
| Authorization status | approved |
| Type lets the patient move the authorization | yes |
| New provider's kind | listed for the type |
| New provider's specialty | same as the original servicing provider |
| New provider's location | in the residence service area, or outside it with the patient accepting that the access standards no longer bind |
| New provider has already declined the patient | no |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

An approved Rehabilitative Therapy Referral with 8 of 12 visits remaining and a span ending on 30 May is moved on 10 April to another network physical therapy practice in the patient's residence service area. From 10 April the new practice is the servicing provider; 8 visits remain and the span still ends on 30 May.
